newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia April housing finance up 12.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia April housing finance up 12.2 pct.

text.p: Finance commitments for owner-occupied housing in Australia rose 12.2 percent by volume to 43,595 dwellings in April from a March level of 38,862, seasonally-adjusted, the Australian Bureau of Statistics said.
In value terms, housing finance rose to A$4.62 billion in April from A$4.18 billion in March, the bureau said.
Analysts forecasts had centred on a rise of 12.0 percent in volume commitments for April.

The bureau said finance commitments for the construction of dwellings rose 12.1 percent, commitments for the purchase of established dwellings rose 11.5 percent and those for the purchase of new dwellings rose 24.3 percent.
The bureau said the number of commitments under new finance, excluding refinancing, rose 6.5 percent in April.
The monthly total number of dwelling unit approvals for a April was the highest since July 1994.
The bureau said that because of the unusual lateness of Easter in March, the seasonal allowance for the effects of Easter might not be sufficient.
"Users should exercise caution in interpreting the March-April movement," it said.
In trend terms, finance commitments rose 1.2 percent in the year to April, while in seasonally adjusted terms, commitments were up 15.6 percent on the year.
